**Not seen on screen.** This machine has no LÖVE, so I have not looked at the weighted picture. It stays off by default until someone does.

Before: a drawn body sat exactly on a straight blend between the two newest snapshots. It had no motion of its own, so when a body changed direction, its drawing changed direction in the same frame (issue 709).

After: every body also gets a drawn position with a velocity of its own. A spring pulls it toward the honest position, and the spring swings a little before it settles. The drawn body leans into a turn, runs slightly past a stop, and comes back. The `i` key switches between the honest picture and the weighted one, and honest is the default. Nothing outside the screen reads these positions: no simulation code, measurement or replay touches them.

## How

- **New module.** `src/074-the-drawn-body.lua` holds the drawn x, y, vx and vy in flat arrays, one slot per body. Over each frame it solves the damped spring exactly toward the honest position, instead of stepping it, so the result does not depend on frame rate. It then keeps the drawn body inside the lag limit.
- **Renderer.** It now draws every body at `where.x[id], where.y[id]` and no longer chooses the position itself. `interpolated_position` is now exported, alongside a new `place_honestly`.
- **Viewer.** Each frame it fills both pictures and passes the renderer the one that `state.weighted` selects.
- **Input.** `i` toggles `state.weighted`.

## Decisions

- **R2, the spring's numbers, are provisional.** I chose 3 swings a second and a damping ratio of 0.5. At 60 fps the drawn body trails a hurrying body by about 2.2 paces, overruns a stop by under 1 pace, and settles within about 0.65 s. I picked these by arithmetic. Because they have not been looked at, the weighted picture is off by default, and the issue file says so.
- **R3 (a body placed rather than walked) is settled: it snaps** to its true position with zero velocity. That happens when:
  - it was not alive, or not being followed, in the previous frame;
  - it moved more than one `personal_space` in a single tick (the fastest walk is under 2 paces a tick);
  - the game is running faster than walking pace.
- **A hard bound sits behind those rules.** The drawn position is never more than half a `personal_space` (9 paces) from the honest one, so a body can never be drawn past a neighbour it did not pass.
- **The weighted picture breaks "never ahead" on purpose.** Overrunning a stop is exactly what 709 asks for. `docs/017` and the viewer info now name this as the one exception, and it is bounded and opt-in.
- **Step 3 (shared memory) and R4 are left alone,** as the issue itself advises.
- **The tests go in `051-the-invariants` with their own `-- covers: 709` line, not in the header.** That keeps clear of #146, which edits the header. The census reads every covers line in a file.
- **This takes file number 074.** #154 takes 073, so the counter file conflicts with #154 on one line; the right value is 074. Census text: this branch says 60, #146 says 61 and #154 says 63. After all three merge it should read 66 of 80.

## Tested

- **Invariants: 95 passed, 6 failed.** The 6 failures are the same ones that fail on `origin/main`. Eleven checks are new and all pass:
  - a walking body is trailed and never led;
  - a stop is overrun, then the body settles;
  - the swing comes out identical, within 1e-6, at 30 and 150 fps;
  - the lag bound holds;
  - snapping happens at birth, on a teleport, above walking pace and when a slot is reused, and does not happen for a body that walks a pace.
- **Mutations:** removing the lag bound, or removing the teleport rule, each makes its own check fail.

Stacked on #153 (`claude/sdc-units`), because domains and movement need the unit row and the catalogue. Issues 203 and 204 of supcom-derivative-clone's phase 2.

**Before:** a unit had a domain but nothing read it. A tank could be put in the sea, and nothing moved: the tick's move row was a placeholder.

**After:**
- One question decides where a unit may stand: land at or above the water line, sea below it, air anywhere. A tank cannot be spawned in the sea, and the world's validator refuses one it finds there.
- A plane flies at the ground beneath it plus its flight height.
- Units walk their pattern one point at a time and hold after the last. They are slower uphill and stop at the water, and a tank walks round another tank in its way instead of through it. Planes are left to their missions.

**How:** two new modules.
- `src/042-domains.lua` holds a dispatch table, `STAND`, with one function per domain. It also has `can_stand`, `altitude_at`, `ground_at`, `is_shore` and a row validator.
- `src/043-movement.lua` has `move_pass` and `move_pass_slice` (the tick's sliceable move row), `occupancy_pass`, `step_length` and `held`.

The world gains a pattern store, `world.pattern = {count, points}`, which the hash, the snapshot copy and the validator all cover. It also gains two columns: `waited` on units and `occupant` on cells. The catalogue gains a per-kind `climb`.

**Decisions**
- **The pattern store's shape:** `points[n]` is a list of `{x, y}`, as the test and the tests document write it, not the issue's flat array.
- **`leg` is the point the unit is heading for**, counting from 1; one past the last means it holds (A4's working ruling). A step that would pass a point lands on it exactly, and the leftover distance is not carried.
- **Slope (C1's working ruling, both):** a step is `speed / (1 + climb * rise)`, the rise measured a whole cell ahead. `climb` is 0.5 for the tank, 0.3 for the enforcer, and 0 for kinds that do not walk. Downhill is never faster than flat, and a ship's water is flat.
- **Occupancy is rewritten at the start of the whole-world move pass**, not by a new row at the tick's end, because phase 1's test fixes the tick at 13 rows. A slice never writes it; the thread pool (209) must run `occupancy_pass` before slicing.
- **Going round a held cell:** wait one pass, then step square to the way, left first, until past. I tried turning 45° first and it left a unit nudging the corner for ever. Only land units hold cells.
- **Spawn refuses a unit where its domain may not stand** (201 left this to 203). Every spawn point in the tests is land on the pinned seed and on five others I tried.
- **Over the sea a plane flies above the water line**, not the sea floor. A shore cell is land with sea in one of its 4 neighbours.
- Domains loads the units module only inside `altitude_at`, so the two never load each other in a circle.

**Tests:** `./run-tests`, phase 2 program (020): 89 held. All 8 failures are named absences for issues 205–211. The phase 1 program (019) still holds 150 of 150. The given suites pass: three domains, and a pattern walked and held on the pinned seed's real dunes. New suites:
- the dispatch table, refusals off the field, shore cells, plane altitude over dune and sea, no tank spawned in the sea, and the validator naming a tank found in it;
- the water is a wall (stops at the shore, keeps its leg), uphill is slower, downhill is never faster, and ships' water is flat;
- two tanks: the walker waits, never enters the held cell, goes round, and reaches its end;
- planes ignore patterns, the move row is wired and sliceable, patterns are in the hash and the copy, and an unknown pattern is refused.

`./validate-documentation`: 0 problems. `./compile --check-only`: 27 files, 0 broken. `./run-headless --ticks 10000` now takes about 0.5 s, up from 0.3; the extra is the occupancy clear and the new columns in the hash.

This branch is stacked on `claude/039-extra-roots` (#150) and also merges in `claude/053-shared-components` (#126) and `claude/040-claudemd-revisions` (#119), because it needs the stand-in model and the 056 issue edits from both stacks. Until those merge, this diff shows their changes too. Once they are in, set this PR's base back to `main` before merging it.

### Before
Saved conversations had no summary, and most are longer than the local model can read at once. Issue 056 specified a recursive summariser (056b), and nothing implemented it.

### After
`scripts/summarize-transcript.lua TRANSCRIPT` packs the transcript into slices that fit the model. It summarises each slice, then merges the summaries level by level until one is left, logging each level's fan-in. It then asks for a one-sentence title and a table-of-contents paragraph, and makes a slug from the title. It changes no file; it prints a small plain record, or JSON, for the 056c applier. `--plan` shows the slicing before the model is asked anything.

### How
- Token counts come from the server's `/tokenize`, through the existing 056a client.
- Slices hold at most `context − reserve − overhead` tokens. The defaults are 16384, 1024 and 512, matching the words-pdf llama.cpp server.
- Exchanges are packed greedily, and summaries are packed the same way at each merge level.
- The stand-in brain learned `summarize-slice`, `merge-summaries`, `title` and `blurb`, plus `STAND-IN-THINK` to imitate Qwen3's reasoning block.

### Decisions
- **056b first, against the stand-in.** This was 056's decision (#132), taken as final by the coordinator.
- **Slices hold whole exchanges, not just whole turns.** Packing single turns let a slice end on a question whose answer opened the next slice. An exchange too big for a slice is cut between lines, and a line too big for one between words; this is reported.
- **A merge that cannot shrink stops with exit 1.** If no two summaries fit together, another level would change nothing, so the run says to raise `--context` or lower `--reserve`.
- **`<think>` blocks are stripped from every answer.** Qwen3 writes them by default.
- **The output is a plain record** of `name: value` lines plus two headings, so the Bash applier can read it without a JSON parser. `--json` gives the same fields.
- **The title keeps only the first sentence,** without quotes or Markdown. The slug is lowercase ASCII words, at most 60 characters, cut at a word boundary, with `untitled-session` as the fallback.
- **Every failure exits 1 with the step named:** a model error, an unreachable server (with the start command), or a merge that cannot shrink. Usage problems exit 2.

### Tested
- `scripts/test-summarize-transcript.sh` passes 40/40 against the stand-in. The stand-in's `/tokenize` counts words, so small budgets force many slices. It covers:
  - one slice and no merge;
  - `--plan` showing whole exchanges;

  - a `<think>` block;

Files and builds scripts issue 048, routed from delta-version issue 067 (TUI Panel Abstraction Layer), which decided the panels belong in the shared `scripts/libs/tui.lua`.

**Before:** every screen on `tui.lua` (the Lua menu, verdict viewer, delta-version's history viewer) works out absolute screen rows by hand, and nothing keeps one region's text out of the next.

**After:** `tui.create_panel(row, col, width, height)` gives a rectangle with its own row 1, column 1. Writes, clears and invalidations take panel coordinates, and anything outside the panel or the screen is dropped.

## How

- New "Panels" section in `libs/tui.lua`: `set_cell`, `write_str`, `clear`, `clear_row`, `invalidate`, `invalidate_row`, `set_fg`/`set_bg`/`set_attrs`/`reset_style`, `to_screen`, `from_screen`. Every write goes through `tui.set_cell`, so the existing dirty tracking sees panel writes as any other.
- Three hooks so a test needs no terminal: `tui.init_buffers(rows, cols)`, `tui.get_cell(row, col)`, `tui.set_output(fn)` (catches what `present()` sends).
- `libs/tui.info.md` (new), issue 048 filed straight into `issues/completed/` with What Happened.

## Decisions

- **Global style**, 067's recommended option 1.
- **Invalidation marks only the panel's cells**, via `tui.invalidate_region`, instead of 067's whole-row pseudocode, so a narrow panel does not resend its neighbours. A full-width panel still marks whole rows.
- **Clipped to the screen first.** `invalidate_region` clamps off-screen rows onto the last row; a footer hanging off a small terminal would have marked the wrong row. A panel wholly off-screen sends nothing.
- **`clear`/`clear_row` leave the drawing style alone** (`tui.clear_row` resets it as a side effect).
- **Bad sizes refused at creation**; the corner may lie off-screen. Fields are read-only by convention; make a new panel to move one. No overlap or borders, as 067 decided.
- **Not done here:** moving delta-version's `history-viewer.lua` onto panels (067's step 9), left for a later PR as asked; moving `menu.lua` onto panels is noted as a possible issue.

## Tested

- `luajit scripts/tests/test_tui-panels.lua "$PWD/scripts"`: 44 checks pass, three runs (present sends single cells in `pairs` order, so the test checks where each character lands, not the order). On main it fails (no `init_buffers`/`create_panel`).
- `bash scripts/libs/test-menu-screen.sh "$PWD/scripts/libs"`: 7/0, so the menu still draws as before.
- `scripts/validate-issues`: 048 adds no findings.

Issue 058, machinery only: seeded, reproducible re-pricing from the balance harness's win rates. The default prices in `template_costs.lua` are unchanged and stay first guesses; everything this produces is marked provisional. Headless only; nothing was seen on a screen.

## Before
Prices were first guesses with no way to check them against how templates actually fight.

## After
- `src/testing/repricing.lua`:
  - **measure:** a seeded round robin of templates;
  - **calibrate:** a reference template with 0/5/10/20 extra points of health fights the same field, and a line through (points, log-odds) gives points per log-odds;
  - **fair cost:** points used plus log-odds times points per log-odds;
  - **fit:** a damped, clamped factor per body, stat price and ability.
- Every result carries `provisional = true`. Every printed line starts `[provisional]` and says nothing was applied.
- `./run <dir> reprice` runs over all 21 defaults in about a minute and writes nothing.
- Issue 058 records the Round 4 decision (tune only after 067) and stays open; the roadmap notes the machinery.

## How
It reuses `AbilityBalance.round_robin`/`matchup` (seeded Park–Miller randomness). Parts come from each template's cost breakdown, and a template's gap is shared across its parts by their share of its cost.

## Decisions
- Balance is not tuned against the harness's walk-straight stand-in. Tuning waits for 067 (coordinator, Round 4; also in 055 on #124).
- Calibration is against the field, not a mirror match. A mirror is far too sensitive: one point bought about 80% of wins.
- Win rates are smoothed (half a win each side), so 0% and 100% stay finite. With no measurable effect it falls back to 20 points per log-odds and says so.
- Factors are per part, not per template, so fixing an ability moves every template that uses it. Parts with under 0.5 of total cost share stay at 1.
- One damped step (half way, clamped 0.5–2) rather than a full solve: most abilities sit on one or two templates, so a full solve would chase noise.
- The sketch's formula-based `BalanceCalculator` isn't built. The harness measures effectiveness directly.
- No acceptance boxes are ticked; each one is about the prices being right.

## Tested
- `tests/test_repricing.lua`, 7 tests:
  - fit direction on made-up rates;
  - clamping, held parts and even results;
  - suggested prices;
  - every line provisional;
  - calibration (and its fallback);
  - same seed gives the same output;
  - `template_costs.lua` values unchanged after a full run.
- Passes under luajit and lua5.4, with output byte-identical between the two.
- `./run <dir> unit`: all pass; the only ✗ is "LÖVE 2D not found".
- One `./run <dir> reprice` run, not acted on:
  - ranged starters and Fortress are underpriced;
  - Glass Cannon wins 0%, because its power strike needs melee reach on a ranged body.

**Merge notes:**
- Like #109, this PR conflicts with #64/#88 on one line of `issues/progress.md` (the 605 and 606 rows). Keep both rows' new text.
- `issues/603-…md` still links to `issues/609-shared-map-and-model-list.md`. I left it, because the storage stack rewrites that part of 603. Once both are in, point it at `issues/completed/…`.
- `phase-6-progress.md` isn't regenerated here. Rerun `scripts/phase-progress-files.lua` after the phase 6 PRs are in.

## Before

Issue 609 was open. There was no way to let a playmate see your models for a map.

## After

- **`src/share/list.lua`** handles the list itself.
  - `build` makes a list from the sharer's pack and the map. It takes art and sound only and names what it left out. A unit type entry names its model.
  - `encode` writes the list as the issue's Lua table. `decode` reads it back without running it.
  - `missing` gives the hashes the receiver lacks. `bundle` copies just those files, named by hash.
- **`src/share/profile.lua`** is the receiver's side.
  - `verify` checks every arriving file against its hash, and `apply` stores the files once. One bad or unsent file refuses the whole list, and nothing is applied.
  - The files become a layer in front of the player's packs for one game (`attach`). Afterwards `revert` removes it, or `keep` turns it into the player's own pack.
  - `trust` remembers "always from this player" and "always for this map".
- **`src/assets/loader.lua`** gains `push_layer` and `pop_layer`.
- **`src/cli/share.lua`** runs the four file steps: `make`, `missing`, `bundle` and `check`.
- 609 moves to completed. **609a** is filed for the rmail glue and the in-game prompt.

## Decisions

1. **Art and sound only** (answers open question 1). A list never carries unit tables, scripts or map object files, so two players' games can't differ.
2. **A received list is never run.** It is read by a small reader that accepts only plain data. Another player's file can't run code, loop forever or fill memory; the tests try each of these.
3. **One bad file refuses the whole list.** Applying the rest would give a mix neither player chose.
4. **Files, not rmail, for now (safe default).** rmail isn't in this repository, so its formats, and whether a hook can answer its consent step, can't be checked here. Nothing touches the network. 609a carries the rest and **needs rmail's docs**.
5. **The profile is a loader layer.** `keep` re-links its files as a pack so the store's references stay correct.
6. **Lists aren't published in the map browser (1001) yet** (answers open question 2).

## Tested

- `test_share.lua`, 58 tests:
  - building, writing and reading a list exactly;
  - a list that tries to run code, loop, nest too deeply or carry data or climbing paths is refused;
  - only missing files are bundled;
  - tampered or unsent files refuse the list;
  - during a game the sharer's grass shows while the receiver's own unit table is unchanged; afterwards the receiver's grass is back and the profile is collected;
  - `keep`, trust, and the tool's commands.
- `test_hotreload`, `test_cache_loader` and `test_dedup` still pass.

### Before
`measure-authorship.lua` puts the human-versus-machine figures on the front page. It had four problems:
- **Pasted file contents.** The fullest transcript exports paste whole files into the model's answers, and the measure keeps the longest copy of each answer. So those files were counted as conversation. One risc-v-university answer measured 24,169 characters in that export, against 1,942 in every other rendering.
- **Files written through tools.** Files the model wrote with its editing tools were not counted anywhere.
- **`notes/CLAUDE.md`.** These files counted as hand-written notes.
- **Hangs on the real monorepo.** It opened every tracked path, including a Wine prefix's link from `com1` to `/dev/ttyS0`, and blocked reading the serial port.

### After
- **File bodies cut.** Pasted file bodies are cut out of answers, so every conversation is measured alike.
- **New git figure.** One pass over git history reports `lines_added_all` and `lines_added_machine_coauthored`. Both count only paths the piles keep, and a commit counts as the model's when its co-author trailer names Claude. The figure stays on its own lines and is never folded into machine-written text.
- **CLAUDE files excluded.** `notes/CLAUDE*.md` leaves the person's pile.
- **Compaction share shown.** Compaction summaries' share of the model's text is printed and added to the JSON, still counted as the machine's.
- **No more hang.** Tracked symlinks are left out, so the measure finishes on the whole tree.
- **Issue closed.** 059 moves to `completed/` with a What Happened section.

Whole monorepo, this branch:
- human-written: 2,266,281 characters;
- machine-written: 11,197,078 characters (compaction summaries 1,637,184 of that);
- chat ratio: 6.20;
- lines added: 4,101,958, of which 4,098,346 came in machine-co-authored commits.

### How
- **The cut.** It starts at the exporter's `**📄 Full content of PATH:**` label and ends only at the exporter's own close: a bare fence after a blank line, as `claude-conversation-exporter.sh` writes it. A pasted Markdown file with fences of its own is therefore cut whole. A heading or separator also ends it. A label with no fence after it is kept as text.
- **The git pass.** It is one `git log --no-merges --no-renames --numstat` pass, reading the `Co-Authored-By` trailer. Each path goes through the same `classify_path` as the piles.

### Decisions
The decisions are 059's, recorded in #132 and taken as final by the coordinator under Ritz's instruction to answer open questions ourselves:
1. Strip file bodies; do not re-export.
2. No co-author split of the tracked source and docs.
3. Leave out `notes/CLAUDE*.md`.
4. Keep the skill list. The exporter is the scripts project's.
5. Compaction stays the machine's, with its share shown.
6. A separate git-lines figure.
7. No token estimate.

Made while building:
- **Only paths the piles keep count for git lines.** Otherwise data dumps and vendored libraries would swamp the figure.
- **Extension-less files are left out of the git figure,** because history cannot say whether one opened with `#!`.
- **Symlinks are left out of the piles** rather than followed, since a link's text is its target's.

**Also fixed:** my first commit here accidentally tracked `delta-version/tmp`, this machine's link to its RAM scratch folder. A later commit untracks it, and the project's `.gitignore` now ignores `/tmp`.

### Tested

  - a repository with no commits;

body:
**Before:** a tower guard was the last body in hero-less-moba that moved a different way. Its position was an edge and a fraction plus an offset, and it walked the graph node by node. And, it turns out, it never walked at all. Every guard was put out on an edge whose two ends were the same node. The walk skipped an edge of length nought rather than divide by it, so the guard never crossed a node and never asked where to go next. No guard in any match ever patrolled or closed on anything. The scenario that recorded "no guard ever leashes" as a fact about ordinary play was recording this.

**After:** a guard's position is its x and y. Its three ways of moving are rows in the pattern table, ahead of every other row: `patrol` (relax), `leash` (hurry) and `chase` (hurry). They go through the same goal-and-step layers as everything else. Guards now patrol their ground: a lane guard up to the 128-pace edge of its leash, and a base guard across the base interior. A guard chasing something walks to the end of its rope and waits there. Being dragged past the rope still trips the leash, and the guard then walks home refusing every target. The step layer is now used by every body (issue 216d).

**How:** `034-walking` loses the edge walk (`step`, `position_of`, `mode_of`, the `next_node` table) and gains three functions. `arrived_at_node` is the one definition of reaching a node: within a body's room of it, measured from the face of any live building on that node. `next_patrol_node` is the old wander pick. `round_the_stone` aims at a building's side when the straight line to the goal runs through it. `072-the-movement-patterns` gets the three rows. The brain chooses them for guards. `040-structures` gets `leash_radius`, the one answer that the leash pass, the patrol and the chase all use. The `offset_x` and `offset_y` fields are gone from the world record.

Walking guards turned up three more faults, all fixed:
- **A base guard could never get home.** "Home" was 18 paces from the leash node. A base guard is leashed to a library 21 paces in radius, so the masonry held it 25 paces out.
- **A guard that picked the node on the far side of its own tower stood at the wall.** It was dead in line with the tower and its goal. Head-on, the push out of stone has no sideways in it. One guard stood there for 3,000 ticks.
- **The reading that counts bodies inside stone was stricter than the rule.** The push out of stone allows a 1e-6 hair, and the reading did not. It now allows the same hair, as the overlaps reading already did.

**Decisions**
- **M6, does a guard need the graph?** Only `patrol` keeps it. Wandering node to node keeps guards on the built roads and keeps the wander stream drawn once per node. `leash` and `chase` aim straight, because both destinations are inside the guard's own ground.
- **M7, what is the offset for?** Nothing, so it is deleted. Its only reader was the edge walk. `wander_node` is also never read or written; I left it alone as out of scope.
- **Where a chase stops.** The goal is pulled back to the leash radius minus one `personal_space` (18 paces). Issue 304 says "it will not follow that thing out" and asks for an edge that is "a hard line". The margin keeps a jostled guard from flickering in and out of the leash state.
- **Going round stone is the pattern's job, not the step layer's.** Only stone counts here, because it never moves. Bodies stay the step layer's question (H18 is untouched).

**Tested:** `./run-tests` on the branch and on a clean `origin/main`.
- **Docs:** 0 problems.
- **Invariants:** 101 passed and 6 failed. The 6 are the same checks that fail on main. Their numbers differ because guards now move.
- **"The chest was actually used" is rewritten, not loosened.** It used to require `placed > 60` at the end of the match. On this branch it failed with 56, because with the pinned seed the match ends at tick 7,246 instead of 14,484. I checked whether the chest stopped being used, which would be a regression, or whether the count only fit the old match length, which would be an artifact. I sampled every 1,000 ticks on both branches:
  - The placement rate is the same. Main has 54 placed by tick 7,000. This branch has 56 placed by tick 7,246.
  - 56 of the 69 stones drawn left a chest, about four in five.
  - So it was an artifact. The check now tests what it was meant to: more than half of all stones drawn left a chest, with at least 20 drawn.
  - A passive match on the same seed draws 75 stones, places none, and fails the new check. The played match passes it.
- **Scenes:** the same 2 claims fail as on main. One of them, guards inside masonry, now counts 4 where main counts 1. Walking guards get pinned against walls by crowds, by up to 0.68 paces. The scenario's comment now says so.
- **Five new invariant checks**, covering 216d and 304. Breaking `round_the_stone` or the home test on purpose makes the matching check fail. The census goes from 59 to 61 of 80.

**Balance note for H18/H19.** No balance was tuned here: leash and chase are as built. Even so, moving guards change how a match plays:
- With the pinned seed (20260826), the match now ends at tick 7,246 instead of 14,484, twice as fast.
- It is also a rout. By the end, team 1 had drawn 8 stones and team 2 had drawn 61; on main they drew 56 and 90.
- Across the 8 other seeds (11 to 88), mean match length went from about 9,600 ticks to about 10,700. So "faster" is true for the pinned seed, not for every match.

Whoever answers H18/H19 should look at this before trusting balance figures measured on the old, frozen guards.

Not seen on screen. I have only measured it headless.

Stacked on #140 (`claude/sdc-territory`). The census needs territory's source to exist to show it failing, and the demo needs everything phase 1 built. Issue 113, the last of supcom-derivative-clone's phase 1. With it, the whole phase is built.

**Before:** the validator only *counted* how many issues had a test, even once source existed. The harness had no way to hand a test a world. Phase 1 had no demo, and `./run-phase-demo` said none had been built.

**After:** source with no test is a failure. If a stem from the tests document's contract table has a file in `src/` or `assets/`, and no test's covers line names the issue that owns it, `./validate-documentation` fails and names the stem and the issue. The harness has `fresh_world(parameters, modules)`. `./run-phase-demo 1` runs phase 1's demo, which does four things:
- runs the phase's checks;
- plays ten thousand ticks on one seed twice and prints the same hash;
- replays the first run's log (1000 fingerprints checked);
- draws the dunes and the water line.

**How:**
- The census reads the contract table where it lives, in docs/014; it keeps no second copy.
- `fresh_world` calls the tick's `assemble`, the same way a match builds its world.
- The demo is a Bash script in `issues/completed/demos/`, built from the existing `run-tests` and `run-headless`.
- Phase 1's program gains three suites:
  - the census, checked on a scratch copy of the project so the real covers lines are never edited;
  - `fresh_world`;
  - a regression test for the bare-name loading bug fixed earlier in the phase.

**Decisions**
- **A stem's owner is the first issue its row names**, the one that creates the file and the one the harness names in an absence. Later issues that only add exports stay counted, not failed. That keeps the rule's "under-claim on purpose".
- **Files in `assets/` count as source** (`the-rules`).
- **The report stays `finish()`.** The issue's table said `report()`, but all ten programs call `finish()`, so I changed the docs, not the code.
- **The demo stops on any failed claim, any problem in the written checks, or any phase 1 absence.** It prints a later phase's absence by name and carries on. Stacked on #117 (`claude/soren-ds-append-writes`), because the test also interrupts appends.

## Before
Writes on the card (405, 406, 413) were meant to leave a file old or new, never torn, but this rested only on the order of the writes. Nothing could interrupt a write to check it.

## After
- The twin has two new functions in `twin/026-platform-twin.{c,h}`:
  - `twin_card_pull_after(n)` lets `n` more blocks land, then fails every read and write as if the card had left the slot. If the cut-off falls inside a write of several blocks, only part of that write lands. A negative count puts the card back, and `twin_card_open` also puts it back.
  - `twin_card_blocks_written()` counts the blocks written, so a test can measure what one operation costs.
- New test `twin/tests/093-test-interrupted-writes.c` uses both to interrupt a write after every block it writes.

## How
Each kind of write first runs once uninterrupted, to count its blocks. Then, for every count from 0 up to that total, the test:
1. puts back the saved card,
2. starts the write with the card set to pull after that many blocks,
3. remounts afresh and checks the file.

| Write | Blocks | Pulled with the file still old | Pulled with the file already new |
|---|---|---|---|
| Replace 5000 bytes with 9000 | 53 | 36 | 17 |
| Append 3000 bytes across clusters | 42 | 42 | 0 |
| Append 100 bytes into spare room | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| Make a file in two new directories | 62 | 61 | 1 |

Each time, the test checks four things:
- the file is old or new, never torn;
- the write did not report success when it had been interrupted;
- the card still mounts;
- the next append leaves a chain exactly the file's size.

## Decisions
- **The pull fails reads as well as writes,** as a card leaving the slot or a power loss would, rather than failing one write and carrying on.
- **A multi-block write lands block by block up to the cut-off,** so a torn table flush is part of what the test covers.
- **The hook is twin-only.** The device's card has no such switch, and `platform.h` is unchanged.
- **I did not regenerate `026-platform-twin.{c,h}.info.md`** to avoid conflicting with #20, which also edits those files. They should be regenerated once both have merged.

## Tested
- 093 passes all 22 checks.
- Mutation checks: writing an append's size before its clusters gives 25 torn files, and ignoring a failed table write gives 16 writes that reported success after being interrupted.
- The full twin suite (14 programs) passes in debug and fast.
- One run out of seven had two failures, in 049 and 075. Those are timing tests that fail under machine load (load average about 7). They don't touch the card and passed on rerun.
- ASan (gcc, with `use_sigaltstack=0`) is clean on 081, 092 and 093.
- I did not rebuild the kernel, since this PR changes only twin and test files.

Stacked on #134 (`claude/sdc-runner-and-viewer`), because it needs the world, the tick, the claim counter and the snapshot hash from the PRs below it. Issue 112, the last mechanic of supcom-derivative-clone's phase 1.

**Before:** no cell had an owner. The tick's claim row was a placeholder waiting for issue 112, and nothing in the economy had a territory percentage to read.

**After:** every land cell has an owner. A team that stands alone near a cell for the claim's length takes it. Two teams near the same cell contest it, and it changes hands to nobody. Water is never claimed. `percent(world, team)` gives the share of land a team holds, the number the economy issues will read.

**How:** a new `src/039-territory.lua`. `claim(world, team, x, y, radius)` sets the team's bit on every land cell within the radius and queues each cell the first time it is marked. `claim_pass` marks around every live unit in array order, then resolves only the queued cells, reading the bits rather than the order of marking:
- one team alone starts or continues a claim, and it completes after `increments_to_claim` increments of the claim counter;
- several teams make a contest.

Once per claim increment, a sweep clears claims nobody has stood near for a whole claim length. The tick's sixth row now runs `territory.claim_pass`. The world's cell group gains `claim_seen` and a per-tick `mark`, and the world gains a `marked` queue; both are empty between passes, so fingerprints never see half a pass.

**Decisions**
- **C4 (pause) is built as a real pause.** The working ruling said the start increment is "kept" during a contest. Kept unmoved, the contest's time would count, and the claim would finish the moment the contest ended. So the start moves on by the increments the contest lasted. I reworded the ruling in docs/016 to say this; the question stays open for you.
- **Walking away pauses too, and a whole claim length away clears the claim**, as the issue's third open point had it.
- **An owner standing alone on its own cell ends another team's claim there**, instead of starting a claim on ground it already holds.
- **The claimant field keeps the name `claim_by`**, which issue 104 laid down and docs/014 names, not the issue's `claiming`.
- **B6:** every unit claims with the rules' `claim_radius` (2) for now. A kind's own radius (the enforcer's 4, a plane's none) belongs in the unit catalogue (202/211).
- **Within the radius means centre to centre**: dx²+dy² ≤ r².
- **`percent` runs from 0 to 100**, over land cells only. Team 0 means the land nobody holds.
- At most 30 teams, because a mark is one bit per team in an int32.

**Tests:** `./run-tests` on phase 1 (`tests/019`): 131 held, 1 not. The one is the original territory suite, which spawns a tank and so waits for `units` (issue 201). Six new suites call `claim` directly:
- a claim completes exactly at its length, and water is never marked;
- a contest neither runs on nor starts over;
- a short absence is paused, and a whole length away clears the claim;
- an owner's return ends an enemy claim;
- the same marks in either order hash the same;
- the tick's sixth row is wired, and bad teams, radii and cells are refused.

I checked by mutation that each pause and clear check fails when its line is removed. `./validate-documentation`: 0 problems. `./compile --check-only`: 23 files, 0 broken. `./run-headless --ticks 10000` takes about 0.35 s, as before.

Issue 602 was open. Nothing drew a missing model's place, a blank map's ground, or the debug view of regions and cameras.

## After

- **`src/assets/fallback.lua`** builds the wire-frame view as data: geometry-kit primitives plus a list of labels.
  - Each object kind gets its own colour and shape, with a letter over it:
    - unit: box, U; flyer: box at fly height with a line to the ground, U; building: large box, B; hero: box, H; item: small box, I;
    - tree: /|\; doodad: an asterisk.
  - Regions are dashed outlines with their names. Cameras have a line to their target. Waypoints are diamonds.
  - A selected object gets a second, thicker green box.
  - The debug overlay adds type, id and coordinates.
  - Terrain is a grid at the ground's height, with lines wider where the ground is higher.
  - `F:texture` and `F:model` go through the loader. A missing texture becomes a checkerboard. `F:is_active(path)` says which paths use the fallback.
  - Also: `force_wireframe`, `register(kind, fn)` for custom painters, `blank(w, h)`, `emit` (through `render.geo_*`) and `draw_labels` (through `render.ui_text` and `viewer.to_screen`).

- 602 moves to completed. **602a** is filed to switch the map viewer and the editor over.

## Decisions

1. **Shapes are data, painted by existing calls.** A line is one thin quad painted through geometry painting (544a; backface culling is off), so no C changed. Raylib isn't built here, so no C could be compiled or seen anyway.
2. **One quad per line.** It lies flat for lines along the ground and stands upright, facing south, for vertical edges. A 128×128 map's grid is about 33k quads, inside the 400k static limit. `every` thins larger maps.
3. **Height:** lines sit at the ground's height and are up to twice as wide on high ground.
4. **No region fill:** geometry painting takes no alpha, and an opaque fill would hide the units inside.
5. **Labels use raylib's built-in font**, so no font asset is needed.
6. **A hero is a type id starting with a capital letter**, as in WC3.
7. **One fallback per caller**, as with the loader.
8. **The viewer and editor aren't switched over here** (602a). That is a visual change to check on a screen.

**Unseen:** nothing here has been looked at on a screen.

Issue 060: saving and loading unit templates. Headless only: **nothing was seen on screen.** The LÖVE file backend was written but not run, since there is no LÖVE here.

**Merge order:** … #124 → #128 → #131 → **this PR**. The base is `claude/rpg-059-template-validation` (#131).

## Before
Templates (#128, #131) existed only in memory. `to_save_data()` produced plain tables, but nothing wrote them anywhere. There were no categories, backups, sharing or search.

## After
- **`src/storage/template_storage.lua`:**
  - save, load, list and delete templates in the **user**, **default** and **imported** categories, one JSON file each;
  - automatic **backups** before every overwrite or delete (newest five kept), with restore;
  - **export** to text and **import** from it;
  - **format migration**, and an index that rebuilds itself if damaged.
- **`src/storage/template_library.lua`:**
  - ranked word search over names, ability names, tags, body and description;
  - filters by category, body, ability, favourites and points;
  - **favourites**, a **recent** list and **use counts**, kept in `library_preferences.json`.
- **`src/storage/file_backends.lua`:** LÖVE's save folder, plain files, or memory, behind one small interface.
- **`TemplateManager`** gains `save_to_storage` and `load_from_storage`. Defaults go to "default" and others to "user".

## How
- **The file envelope** holds `format`, `format_version`, `game_version`, `saved_at`, the template's `to_save_data()`, and metadata (author, description, tags).
- **The index** (`template_index.json`) lists each template's file, body, points, ability names, description and tags, so listing and search never open the files.
- **Slugs:** files are named by slug (letters, digits, hyphens). Colliding slugs get numbered.

## Decisions
- **dkjson,** already vendored in `libs/dkjson/`, does the JSON. No new library.
- **An index file,** because plain Lua can't list folders. LÖVE and memory can, so a damaged index is rebuilt there, with a warning.
- **Compatibility:**
  - Numbered migrations move older files forward. Format 0 reads both a bare `to_save_data()` table and the sketch's `{template_version, template_data}` shape.
  - Newer formats load with a warning.
  - Templates that fail today's rules still load, with "No longer valid" warnings, so they can be fixed rather than lost.
- **Imports never overwrite.** A taken name gets " 2", " 3", since names allow no brackets (#131).
- **Loading never writes.** The sketch rewrote each file on load to count uses. Counts live in library preferences, via `library:use`.
- **Five backups per template.** A deleted template can be restored.
- **The library sits in `src/storage/`,** not `src/systems/` (that folder is ECS systems).
- **The disk backend uses `mkdir -p`,** only on the storage's own fixed folder names, never on template names.

Stacked on #129 (commands and snapshots), because the runner records and replays through the snapshot and the door. The base is that branch, so this diff shows only 110 and 111.

Before: the pieces of a match existed, but nothing played one end to end and nothing could show you the field.

After: `./run-headless` plays a match with no window and prints a report: seed, ticks, final fingerprint, what ended it, wall time, sightline questions, and where the replay log went (in `/dev/shm/supcom-derivative-clone/replays/`). `./run-headless --replay <log>` replays a log into a fresh world and names the first tick whose hash disagrees (exit 1). `--draw` prints the last tick through the new terminal viewer: dunes graded by height, water as `~`, units, a legend, team colours with `--colour`. The phase 1 program holds 106 claims; the one suite still failing is territory, absent by name. Issues 110 and 111 are completed.

How: `src/037-headless-runner.lua` reads `input/seed`, `input/field` and `input/players` (both new, each documenting its own shape), assembles through the tick, records via the snapshot, plays with `advance_timed` (a twin of `advance` that only reads the clock per row), and writes `output/goodbye` last. `src/038-terminal-viewer.lua` reads a snapshot and nothing else. `run-headless` passes options through the environment so nothing typed is spliced into Lua code.

Decisions
- **Replay lives in the runner** (`options.replay`), since issue 109 describes exactly that runner. A log whose stamp differs from the match it would make is refused.
- **Seed precedence follows the issue**: `SDC_SEED` beats `--seed`, which beats `input/seed`; a replay plays its own seed and refuses a different one. `random` takes four bytes from `/dev/urandom` and appends the seed to `seeds.log` in the RAM tier.
- **The runner requires `ticks`**; `./run-headless` passes 10,000 (the phase demo's number) when not told, and says so in its header.
- **The runner's unit capacity is a rule** (`units = 1024` in `assets/034-the-rules.lua`).
- **Wall time uses the monotonic clock via FFI**, since Lua's clocks are whole seconds or processor time.
- **`factories` and `shortest_pattern` report zero** until 307 and 308 exist; the contract table names them.
- **Unit letters wait for the catalogue (202)**: `LETTERS` is empty and a unit draws as `?`, loudly. Land is graded against the field's own highest cell. The viewer counts territory itself, because the viewer rule forbids calling the territory module.
- The phase 1 demo is left for the phase's last issue (113).

Tested: `./run-tests` (validator 0 problems; phase 1 program 106 held, 1 absent; 020 to 027 fail only by absence) on seeds 20260912 and 3; `./compile --check-only` (22 files). New suites: one seed twice gives one hash; a runner's own log replays with 12 hashes checked and no mismatch; a tampered hash at tick 60 is named; a scratch root's malformed field, player and missing lines are refused by line or name; the viewer draws a unit over water, tints an owned cell only when asked, and leaves the snapshot's hash unchanged. By hand: `./run-headless --ticks 300 --seed 5 --draw`, then `--replay` of its log (exit 0), then the log with one hash edited (exit 1, "a mismatch with the replay at tick 200").

Before: issue 034 made `backup-conversations` fail loudly, but `claude-conversation-exporter.sh` still sourced it and called it with `2>/dev/null ... || true`. That code existed in four copies. A broken export therefore still looked exactly like a project with no conversations. Separately, `scripts/tmp`, the link to the RAM tiers, showed as untracked in `git status`.

After: when the exporter has to make a project's transcripts and the backup tool fails, the tool's own message appears, followed by a line naming the project, the tool and the exit status. `scripts/tmp` is ignored. Issue 034's three open questions are answered, and the issue moves to `issues/completed/`.

## How

- The four copies are replaced by one function, `run_transcript_backup`. It runs the first tool it finds as a program, not sourced: the project's `scripts/backup-conversations --all <project>`, an older project's `backup-conversations.sh`, or the `backup-conversations` beside the exporter. It returns the tool's exit status.
- The tool's output goes to stderr, so `exporter <project> all > backup.md` keeps only the conversations. Before this, the tool's progress lines landed in that file.
- `scripts/.gitignore` contains `/tmp`.
- New `tests/test-conversation-exporter-loud.sh`, with 7 checks. Stand-in backup tools fail, succeed, or are an older `.sh`; none of them reads `~/.claude`.

## Decisions

- **Q1, should the Stop hook run in the background? No.** It would save about 0.75 s a reply, and it isn't established that a background hook's failure is shown as plainly. That visibility is the whole point of 034.
- **Q2, should the exporter stop sourcing the tool? Yes.** It now runs the tool as a program and shows its failures.
  - The fallback tool is the one beside the exporter, not the hard-coded `/home/ritz/...` path. They are the same file on Ritz's machine, but only the exporter's own location is right in every checkout.
  - A failure is reported but doesn't stop the exporter. The caller's next check ("no conversations found") still runs and exits as it did before.
- **Q3, ignore `scripts/tmp`? Yes, in the project's own `.gitignore`.** burner-of-down-things and hero-less-moba do the same for their tmp links. The repository-wide file is generated by delta-version and lives outside this project.

## Tested

- `tests/test-conversation-exporter-loud.sh <scripts-dir>`: 7 passed, 0 failed.
- Against the exporter on main, 3 of the 7 fail: no project or exit status named, the tool not run with `--all <project>`, and the older script's failure not shown.
- `git status` no longer lists `scripts/tmp`.

Issue 059: template validation and constraints. Headless only: **nothing was seen on screen.**

**Merge order:** … #105 → #124 → #128 → **this PR**. The base is `claude/rpg-057-unit-templates` (#128).

## Before
Unit templates (#128) did their own basic checks inside `UnitTemplate:validate`.
- The messages were terse, such as "health must be 50-500, not 10".
- There were no warnings.
- The limits were mixed in with the prices.
- A game mode couldn't change the rules.

## After
- **`src/data/template_constraints.lua`** holds every limit in one place:
  - name length and allowed characters, and description length;
  - hard and comfortable ranges for each stat;
  - ability limits (count, power, range, area, duration, cooldown, mana rate, effects over time, zones, pierce, cleave);
  - the thresholds for warnings.
- **`src/validators/template_validator.lua`:**
  - `validate_template` returns ok, errors and warnings.
  - `validate_detailed` gives each finding's rule and weight.
  - `add_rule` adds a mode's own rule.
- Every message names the thing, the number, the limit and the fix. For example: "Ability 1 (primary_melee_attack): range 300 is over the limit of 100; lower it".

## How
- `UnitTemplate:validate(validator)` hands off to the validator and stores `validation_warnings` next to `validation_errors`.
- Each ability is built once per validation, and the rules read the built ability.
- Rule order is fixed and keys are sorted, so messages come out the same under luajit and lua5.4.
- `template_costs.lua` now holds prices only.

## Decisions
- **What is an error and what is a warning:**
  - Errors: name, unit type, stat ranges, ability count, ability limits, primary kind, budget.
  - Warnings: odd stats, three of a kind, repeats, long reach on melee or tank bodies, heavy armor on a ranged body, spending under half the budget.
- **"Covers all critical game balance aspects" stays unticked.** Whether a legal template is too strong belongs to 058. Tuning waits for 067, per the Round 4 decision now recorded in 055.
- **Limits are in this game's units** (maximum reach 100, where ranged is about 30), not the sketch's.
- **The sketch's stat-percentage rule is replaced by per-stat comfortable ranges.** The sketch summed health, speed and range, which mixes units.
- **No `effect_type` / `target_type` checks.** Templates use the ability system's kinds, and building the ability proves it valid.
- **Zero-duration buffs are legal.** The kind gives them 5 s.
- **Some defaults carry warnings, and that's allowed.** The brute has three debuffs, the skirmisher three damage abilities, and the berserker spends 41 points. 061 revisits the defaults.

## Tested
- `tests/test_template_validation.lua` (9 tests) is new, and is added to `./run <dir> unit`. It covers:
  - names, stats, abilities, budget and warnings;
  - configurable and added rules;
  - every default being valid;
  - 1000 validations taking 0.06 s under luajit and 0.12 s under lua5.4.
- The 057 tests now look for the new wording of the same checks. Nothing was loosened.
- Both interpreters pass.
- `./run <dir> unit`: the only ✗ is "LÖVE 2D not found".
- Nothing was drawn or seen.

Before: issue 007's switch to plain HTML was done in December, but the issue was still open and the page didn't fully live up to "no CSS, no JavaScript". There were five gaps:
- A file called `<script>alert(1)<.md` was written into the page raw, so it became a `<script>` element.
- A folder called `$(touch x)` ran `touch x` during the scan. Paths went to `find`, `du` and `stat` in double quotes. I saw this happen with the old library.
- Links broke on spaces, `#` and quotes.
- The runner loaded its library from under the folder being scanned, so it failed on any folder other than the monorepo. It also read `-o` as the folder when `-o` came first.
- The library README still described a sidebar, live search and a dkjson dependency.

After: every name is shown as text in the page and nothing in a name ever runs. Links are percent-encoded, the runner works on any folder, and both READMEs describe the page as it is. Issue 007 moves to `issues/completed/` with a What Happened section.

## How

- `libs/project-file-server.lua` has three new helpers:
  - `shell_quote`: single quotes, used for every path given to the shell.
  - `html_escape`: used for every name, and for links.
  - `file_url`: percent-encodes everything except letters, digits, `-._~/`.
- `find -path "<dir>"` became `-mindepth 1`, because `-path` read the folder name as a pattern.
- The shebang is now `luajit`, and the unused `package.path`/dkjson setup is gone.
- `project-file-server`:
  - Finds the library beside itself (`readlink -f`) and runs it with `luajit`.
  - The first plain word is the folder and the second is the output (`-o` also works).
  - The default output is worked out after all arguments are read.
  - An unknown option or a missing folder is refused with exit 1.
- New `tests/test-project-file-server.sh`, with 27 checks.

## Decisions

- **Hostile names are escaped and listed, not skipped.** Leaving them out would hide real files.
- **The "nothing ran" check runs the scan from inside a canary folder.** The hidden `touch` names no folder, so it would write there.
- **The quick links stay hard-coded.** They are Ritz's folders; making them configurable would be a separate issue.
- **The interactive menu's `python3 -m http.server` options stay.** They serve the finished page and add nothing to it.

- Against the runner and library on main, 15 of the 27 fail.
- Run directly on a hostile tree, the old library ran a folder's `$(touch ...)` and wrote raw `<script>` into the page.

Stacked on #122 (the world and the tick), because the door and the snapshot are the tick's first and last rows and live in the world's layout. The base is that branch, so this diff shows only 108 and 109.

Before: the tick ran thirteen rows that all did nothing, there was no way for a player's intent to get in, and nothing could say whether two worlds agreed.

After: every player action comes through one door (`queue`), stamped for a later tick, and the tick's first row applies it in the order queued. A command the door will not take is refused by name, returned to the caller and kept in a ring in the world for a viewer to show. The tick's last row fingerprints the world, and a match can be recorded to a text log and replayed to the same hashes. The phase 1 program holds 84 claims (up from 56); the three suites still failing are absent by name (runner, viewer, territory). Issues 108 and 109 are completed.

How: `src/035-commands.lua` holds `VERBS` (`noop`, `set-energy-level`), `ARGUMENTS`, `queue`, `apply_due`, `refusals`. The world's layout gains a `command` queue (in insertion order, a removed row closes the gap) and a `refusal` ring, and a `text` type for the ring's reasons. `src/036-snapshot.lua` folds every group's arrays as the 32-bit words of their memory (so a double is folded by its bits), copies with `ffi.copy`, stamps the parameters and rules with keys sorted, and reads and writes the log.

Decisions
- **The world is fingerprinted every `fingerprint_every` ticks (ten, one a second), not every tick.** Hashing every tick took 1.1 s per 10,000 ticks on the test's 64x64 field (the test's limit is 2 s) and grows with the field's area; now 0.11 s. The log writes every fingerprint. `docs/003` now says "every so many ticks". If you want every tick for lockstep later, it is one number in the rules.
- **`queue` returns nothing on success**, as the tests and the contract table say, not the issue's "ticket".
- **`set-energy-level` exists now** because the phase 1 test queues it. It only enforces "four buttons, never a fifth" (a fifth is refused at apply time) and sets `energy_level`; what a button means stays issue 302's.
- **Applied commands leave the queue at once.** The recorder writes each command when the door accepts it (issue 109's design), so nothing needs to keep it after.
- **A queued command for a tick already past raises** instead of being dropped: it means a tick ran without the door, and a silently lost command is the worst kind of desync.
- **Refusal reasons are text**, so the layout has a `text` type (Lua strings, empty where nothing), folded into the hash by bytes.
- **The replay stamp covers the allocation parameters and every rule**, so a log recorded before a balance change can be refused; the world now keeps a copy of its parameters.
- A hash line is the fingerprint taken during that tick (`world.fingerprint`, `world.fingerprint_tick`); a replayer compares those, not a fresh hash.

Tested: `./run-tests` (validator 0 problems; phase 1 program 84 held, 3 absent by name; programs 020 to 027 fail only by absence); `./compile --check-only` (20 files). New suites: every refusal reason, the ring's order and capacity, a full queue; a copy that stands alone and still validates; a double one bit apart hashing differently; record, replay into a fresh world, same hash at every logged tick, a different stamp for a different world, a non-replay file refused.

Issue 057: unit templates that players can design within a point budget, priced by the ability system's own abilities. Headless only: **nothing was seen on screen.**

**Merge order:** #63 → #80 → #82 → #90 → #94 → #96 → #101 → #104 → #105 → #124 → **this PR**. The base is `claude/rpg-051-056-reconcile` (#124).

## Before
- Units came from fixed type tables in `src/entities/unit.lua`.
- There was no way to describe a custom unit, price it, check it, or save it.

## After
- **`src/data/unit_template.lua`:** `UnitTemplate.new(data)` holds a body (unit type), stats, 1-4 abilities and a look.
  - Pricing: `calculate_point_cost` gives the total with a breakdown.
  - Checks: `validate` gives plain-language errors.
  - Use: `create_unit(em, x, y, team)` builds a real unit with the template's health, speed, armor, abilities and mana bars.
  - Saving: `to_save_data` and `from_save_data`.
- **`src/data/template_costs.lua`:** every price, the budget (100), the stat ranges and the ability limits, in one file.
- **`src/managers/template_manager.lua`:** register, get, remove and list. It makes one valid default per ability set (eleven, costing 41-96 points).

## How
- **Stat costs:** stats cost points only above the chosen body's own values.
- **Body costs:** melee 0, ranged 10, tank 10, support 0, special 10.
- **Ability costs:** base (primary 10, others 20) × strength, plus 1 point per 5 reach past 15, plus 1 per 10 area radius.
  - Strength is effect per second next to the sword's.
  - It counts crits, accuracy, cleave, pierce, area targets, effects over time and zones.
  - A long cooldown slows the rate.
  - Buffs and debuffs are priced by uptime.

## Decisions
- **Templates list ability-system abilities** (a template name, a name with changes, or a whole config), not the sketch's separate `effect_type`/`base_value` fields. Template units fight exactly like any other.
- **Stats are priced from the body's values, and lowering one refunds nothing.** This avoids dump stats.
- **There are five bodies,** not the sketch's two.
- **The first ability must deal damage or heal,** since it's the always-charging primary.
- **Where files go:**
  - The costs sit in `src/data/`, since there is no `src/config/`.
  - The manager starts `src/managers/`, as the sketch named it.
  - Saving to disk is left to issue 060.
- **All prices are first guesses** for issue 058 to tune.

## Tested
- `tests/test_unit_templates.lua` (8 tests) is new, and is added to `./run <dir> unit`. It covers:
  - body defaults, stat and ability costs, and validation;
  - save and load, and building a unit;
  - the manager;
  - template-built warriors and archers fighting in the balance harness.
- It passes under luajit and lua5.4.

> **Merge #119, #120 and #123 first.** This PR's base is #123's branch (`claude/051-vision-from-history`), so the diff shows only this PR's own changes. No rebase. After #123 merges into main, set this PR's base back to `main` before merging it.

### After
`delta-version/scripts/todone.lua [PROJECT_DIR ...] [--all] [--min=N] [--each] [--json] [--synonyms=FILE]`
- **Scanning (053a):** for each project it reads the titles of open issues and the headings of `docs/roadmap.md`. Completed, `done/` and `archive/` issues and `moved-` pointers are left out.
- **The model's part:** the local model (the existing `libs/llama-chat-client.lua`) names the reusable components each project plans, and leaves out project-specific features.

  - spelling: case, spaces, `-` and `_` are ignored;

- **The report:** components planned by `--min` or more projects (default 2), with those projects. `--each` adds what was found in each project, and `--json` is also available.

Before: a bash `menu.sh` menu taller than the screen ran off the bottom. The terminal clamped the extra rows onto its last line, and the description and footer were drawn over the lower items. A later section never appeared. In a 40-row terminal, pressing G put the cursor on an item that could not be seen.

After: a list taller than its room scrolls inside the box. The header, description and footer stay put, the list shows a window around the cursor, and a scrollbar in the last column shows where that window is. A menu that fits draws exactly as before.

Stacked on #108 (`claude/issue-004-menu-render`), so merge that first. Without #108's footer fix the screen scrolls under the menu and every row is off by one.

## How

- `libs/menu.sh`
  - New `menu_update_viewport`: works out the rows the list has (screen less header, footer, description and separator) and counts the list in lines (title, underline, items, a blank line per section). It then moves `MENU_SCROLL_OFFSET` only as far as needed to keep the cursor's line in view.
  - New `menu_screen_row`: turns a list line into a screen row, or -1 when the line is out of view.
  - New `menu_render_scrollbar`: draws a dim `│` track and a `█` thumb, only while the list scrolls.
  - `menu_render`: clears the row caches on each full draw, so items out of view have no row. An incremental move onto one of them then falls back to a full draw, which scrolls. When the list scrolls, the description area is placed after the window.
  - `menu_render_section`: counts in list lines and skips the lines out of view. Item numbers are still counted for hidden items.
  - The incremental update redraws the scrollbar, because its `ESC[K` clears to the end of the line.
- `libs/test-menu-screen.sh`
  - `run_menu` takes `ROWS` (default 30) and `KEY_DELAY` (default 1). These are the same names #93 uses.
  - A 40-row scene: 30 letters and 10 numbers, which is 46 list lines against 28 rows of room. It is checked at the start, after 26 steps down, after G, and after G then g.
  - The checks cover the window size, the items shown and where the cursor is, the section titles, the order of description and footer, and the scrollbar thumb at top and bottom.
  - The small bash menu is checked to draw no scrollbar.
- The README table and issue 041 (filed in `issues/completed/`) are updated.

## Decisions

- **Minimal scrolling**, as in the Lua menu's section viewports (015): stepping past the bottom scrolls one line.
  - The exception is moving up into a section. If its title fits in the window with the cursor's item, the window shows the title too.
- **A scrolling list stops at its last item.** The blank line after the last section is left out of the scroll range, so G puts the last item on the bottom row and the thumb reaches the bottom.
- **The whole list scrolls as one window, not each section.** The bash menu has no per-section viewport setting, and one window is the smallest change that fixes the overflow.

## Known conflict

This conflicts with #93 in `libs/test-menu-screen.sh`, as #108 already does. Both add scenes and change `run_menu`. To resolve it, keep both sets of scenes. In `run_menu`, keep #93's `VALUES_NAME` and this PR's `ROWS`.

## Tested

- `libs/test-menu-screen.sh <libs-dir>`: 20 passed, 0 failed.
- Against the old `menu.sh`, 9 of the 11 new checks fail.

Reconciles issues 051-056 against the ability stack. Each one is closed as done (naming the PR that did it), narrowed, or has its remaining work built here. Headless only: **nothing was seen on screen or heard.**

**Merge order:** #63 → #80 → #82 → #90 → #94 → #96 → #101 → #104 → #105 → **this PR**. The base is `claude/rpg-045-mana-bar-ui` (#105).

## Before
- Issues 051-056 were open, though the ability stack had already built most of them.
- These were missing:
  - weapon variety;
  - cleave;
  - projectile accuracy and drop-off;
  - emergency healing;
  - lasting area zones;
  - walls inside an area blast;
  - any way to measure balance.

## After
| Issue | Outcome |
|---|---|
| 051 primary attacks | **Closed.** Templates came from #101, closest-target and line-of-sight targeting from #94, and always-charging bars from #80. Weapons, cleave, accuracy and drop-off are built here. |
| 052 healing | **Closed.** The heal kind came from #90 and #101, lowest-health targeting from #94, no-waste mana from #82, and heal over time from #104. The emergency heal is built here. |
| 053 buffs/debuffs | **Closed.** Effects, stacking and stats came from #101, cleanse from #104, targeting from #94, and stun and silence from #96. The weakness curse is added here. |
| 054 area | **Closed.** Falloff came from #90, the best centre from #94, and meteor strike and healing circle from #101. Lasting zones, the static field and walls inside the blast are built here. |
| 055 balance | **Narrowed, stays open.** The harness is built. What's left is tuning, which needs a person's call, and memory profiling. |
| 056 activation | **Closed as a repeat of 048,** done by #96, with mana efficiency from #82. |

The visual and audio criteria of 051-054 move to a **new issue 068**, which draws and plays the effect system's cues.

## How
- **Damage kind** gains:
  - `weapon_type`;
  - `cleave_targets`, `cleave_ratio` and `attack_arc`;
  - `accuracy`;
  - `drop_off_distance` and `drop_off_min`.
- **Effect system:**
  - cleaves after each blow;
  - rolls accuracy for each enemy a projectile reaches (a miss flies on);
  - weakens projectile hits by distance flown;
  - new `add_effect`, `projectile_miss` cue, and `cleave_hits` / `projectile_misses` stats.
- **Persistent effects system:**
  - zones, from `zone_duration`, `zone_interval`, `zone_power` and `zone_modifiers` on area abilities;
  - `get_zones()` for a renderer.
- **Targeting:** with line of sight on, units behind a wall from an area's centre are left out.
- **Conditions:** a new `ally_health_below` condition, backed by `lowest_ally_health(range)` in the unit state.
- **Templates:**
  - weapons: axe, dagger, spear, crossbow, sling and javelin;
  - `emergency_heal`, `weakness_curse` and `static_field`;
  - sets: berserker, crossbowman, field_medic and storm_caller.
- **`src/testing/ability_balance.lua`:** seeded battles with every ability system running, plus `matchup`, `round_robin`, Wilson intervals and `report`.
- **`./run <dir> balance`** prints a full round robin.

## Decisions
- **Weapons are templates.** Their differences are baked into the numbers, not into per-weapon classes.
- **Ranges are scaled to this game** (melee about 15, ranged about 30), not the sketch's 35 and 80.
- **Ranged primaries target the weakest enemy in sight,** to finish kills. Melee keeps the closest.
- **No close-range crit for projectiles.** `critical_chance` already exists.
- **Emergency heal timing:** the bar charges near allies and fires only when an ally is under 30%. The sketch gated it on the healer's own health.
- **No separate buff/debuff manager or area effect manager.** The effect system and the persistent effects system already do those jobs.
- **Static field leaves out chain lightning and mana drain.** It keeps damage and a 40% slow.
- **Zones last their full time** even if the caster dies. The first pulse comes one interval after the cast.
- **Balance flags:** a set is flagged only when its whole 95% interval is past 65% (dominant) or 35% (weak). Draws count half to each side.
- **Stand-in movement:** the harness walks units straight at the nearest enemy, in place of lane following.
- **No numbers were retuned.** The first round robin has the ranged sets well ahead:
  - skirmisher 93%, archer 88%, crossbowman 79%;
  - warrior 23%, druid 21%.

  Tuning against stand-in walking could mislead, so this is left open in 055.

## Tested

Stacked on #64 (605's storage manager). Merge that first, then retarget this to main. It merges cleanly with #88, which sits on #64 beside it.

## Before

Every map and asset pack in the player data folder is a folder of links into one store, `blobs/`. The stored files were ordinary writable files. An editor saving a pack's texture through its link changed that texture for every map and pack sharing it, and the file's name (its hash) no longer matched its bytes.

## After

- A newly stored file is read-only (mode 0444).
- `store:unshare(dest)` (in `dedup.lua`) does copy-on-write. It replaces one link with a private, writable copy of the bytes. The stored file and every other link to it stay as they were, and `gc` collects the stored file once nothing links to it.
- `store:protect()` makes the blobs of an older store read-only and says how many it changed.
- `storage.lua` gains:
  - `S:edit(kind, name[, path])`, for one file, or every link in a map or pack;
  - `S:protect()`.
- The storage tool gains:
  - `edit map|pack NAME [PATH]`, which prints the paths to open in an editor;
  - `protect`.
- The change is recorded as a new completed issue, **604a**. 604 and 605 list it under Blocks, and `progress.md` has a row for it.

## How

The copy is written next to the link and renamed over it. The rename replaces the link itself, never the stored file. The copy keeps the same path, so the loader, hot-reload and references find it with no change, and it counts toward the pack's own bytes.

## Decisions

1. **Ritz's call (2026-11-02):** stored files are read-only, and editing makes a private copy for that pack.
2. **The copy is made on request, not by catching the editor's write.** An outside editor writes straight to the file system, and nothing in the engine sees that write first. The read-only mode makes an ordinary user's write fail; `storage.lua edit` makes the copy to open instead.
3. **Root isn't stopped by the mode.** `verify()` still reports a stored file whose bytes no longer match its hash.
4. **Older stores are fixed with `protect`, not on every open**, so opening a store stays cheap.
5. **`gc` is unchanged.** Removing a file needs its folder to be writable, not the file.
6. `phase-6-progress.md` is not regenerated here, because its count line would collide with #79. Rerun `scripts/phase-progress-files.lua` once the phase 6 PRs are in.

## Tested

- `test_storage.lua` now has 67 tests (20 new). They cover:
  - modes 0444 and 0644;
  - writing the private copy leaves the stored file and two maps unchanged, and the store still verifies;
  - the copy's bytes count as the pack's own; editing it twice does nothing;
  - edit with no path, then gc;
  - refusals: a missing map, `../`, a missing file, and a link that leads outside the store;
  - `protect`, and the tool's `edit` and `protect`;
  - run as `nobody` through `setpriv`: reading through a link works and writing through it is refused.
- `test_dedup.lua` passes (62 tests).
- Full suite: everything passes except `test_net_hosted`, which needs effil, as on main.

Before: a script that sourced `libs/lua-menu.sh` from inside a function lost every menu table when that function returned. This was found in delta-version. After the return, all section titles overwrote each other and the second item was refused as a "Duplicate item_id" of the first. `menu.sh`, `checkbox.sh` and `multistate.sh` broke the same way.

After: all four libraries work whether they are sourced at the top level or from inside a function.

## How

- Every top-level `declare -A` / `declare -a` in `libs/lua-menu.sh`, `libs/menu.sh`, `libs/checkbox.sh` and `libs/multistate.sh` is now `declare -gA` / `declare -ga`. A short comment beside each table block says why.
- `scripts/tests/test-menu-libraries-sourced-in-function.sh` is new, with 49 checks.
  - It sources each library from a function in a fresh bash and checks that every top-level table is still there with the right kind. The list of tables is read from the library itself.
  - It then builds a two-section menu that way with `lua-menu.sh`, checking `_menu_build_json`, and with `menu.sh`, checking its tables.
- Issue 040 is filed straight into `issues/completed/`.

## Decisions

body:
Stacked on #35 (`claude/soren-ds-filesystem-boxes`): the box joins `082-files.c`, which #35 adds.

## Before
One value carries at most 4096 bytes, and `write-path` replaces a file with one value. A program could read a file of any size through `read-slice` but could not write one larger than 4096 bytes. The painter's saved drawings (810) need exactly that.

## After
- New box **`append_path(path, value)`**, with the same inputs as `write_path`. It adds the value's bytes to the end of the file. A missing file is made, along with any directories on its way. Through a symlink, the target grows. A directory is a status in the value.
- A file of any size is now several appends, each whole or not at all. A `read_slice` wired into an `append_path` copies a 10000-byte file in 4096-byte slices.
- Issue 413 is filed and closed in this PR. The docs/011 box list, the 406 note and the phase-4 progress file are updated.

## How
Each append runs in this order, and nothing a reader can see moves until step 4:
1. `fat_chain_append` (077) writes the new bytes into the spare room at the end of the last cluster. No byte of the file lives there.
2. Bytes that don't fit go into new clusters. They are written, then marked as taken in the table while still unlinked.
3. The new clusters are linked onto the chain, and the table is flushed again.
4. `files_append` (078) writes the entry's new size.

If the card is pulled out after step 3, the chain is longer than its file. `fsck.fat` trims the extra clusters, and so does the next append: `fat_chain_cut` lets go of any cluster past the file's last byte before anything is added. On any failure, the chain is cut back to the old size.

## Decisions
- **The 4096-byte cap per value stays, as decided for this round.** A larger file is built from several appends, each within the cap, rather than by growing the value.
- **A box of its own, not a mode flag on `write_path`.** The engine has no optional inputs, so a mode flag would be a third port that every writer had to wire. docs/011 also says anything past the six boxes arrives as a new box when an app needs it.
- **It answers 0 or a negative code, the same as `write_path`.** If the value is a failed read, nothing is appended and its status is passed on. A value claiming more than 4096 bytes is refused.
- **A file built from many appends is not atomic as a whole.** Between appends, the file holds the appends so far. Making a whole file appear at once would need a rename box, which does not exist yet and is not built here.
- **On a full card the answer is `FAT_NO_SPACE`,** and the file and the free space stay as they were.
- **The block holding the file's old end is rewritten with those bytes unchanged.** This is the same single-block risk the directory-entry update already takes. The alternative, copying the last cluster, would move bytes that readers can see.

## Tested
- New `twin/tests/092-test-append.c`: 44 checks. It covers 512- and 4096-byte clusters, appends that cross cluster ends and appends that start exactly at one, and a 195672-byte file built from 120 appends with exact cluster counts and none lost. It also covers appending nothing, appending to an empty file, appending through a link, appending to a directory, a full card, a card left mid-append, two threads appending to one file, the box placed in a map, and a copy in slices.
- Two mutations were each caught by the test: skipping the stray-cluster cut, and skipping the spare-room fill.
- The full twin suite passes in debug and fast (13 programs). ASan (gcc) runs 079, 081, 083 and 092 clean; 092 needs `use_sigaltstack=0` to get past ASan's own thread-exit munmap noise. The aarch64 kernel builds.
- `fsck.fat` is not installed in this environment, so the card-checker checks were skipped.

Before: supcom-derivative-clone had its documents, its issue files, its tools and its tests, and not a line of source. The phase 1 test program reported every subject absent by name.

After: the field exists. `src/028-the-dunes.lua` raises a dune field from a seed and six shape parameters, refuses a field that cannot be played on (naming the cell, team or region), and prints it as text with the water and the start cells marked. `src/029-sightlines.lua` answers "can this point see that one?" over that ground, with no maximum distance. The phase 1 program's dune and sightline suites hold (22 claims), and every other suite still fails by name with the issue that will build it. Issues 102 and 103 are moved to `issues/completed/` by `./complete-issue`, and the phase 1 tracker says built.

How: every cell's height is a 32-bit hash of seed, layer and lattice point (MurmurHash3's finaliser, with a split multiply so C's `uint32_t` gives the same bits), blended between lattice points. Three layers (swell, angled ridges, roughness) plus a causeway that lifts the ground between the two start corners. The sightline runs a coarse pass over each region's tallest cell, then an Amanatides–Woo grid walk that interpolates the segment's height at each crossed cell's centre.

Decisions
- **The test's tall-eye claims were impossible and are corrected, not weakened.** The test stood a tall eye (35) twelve cells before a ridge of 30 and a low target (12) twelve cells after it, and asserted it sees over. The segment crosses the ridge at 23.5, so any walk that follows the dunes document must say no. The claims now put the tall end two cells from the ridge (clears at ~31.7), and the original far geometry is asserted as blocked. A comment in the test explains. **Please look at this one**: it is the only test edit.
- **A causeway layer was added.** As first built, about a third of seeds at the test's shape drowned a start corner or cut the start cells apart, and tuning the water only traded that for fields with no sea. Lifting the ground along the start-to-start diagonal brings refusals to 0 of 1000 seeds (about 1 in 30 has no water at size 64; none at 128). The dunes document and the README say so.
- Positions put a cell's centre at its integer coordinates (`cell_of`). The walk always runs from the end first in row order, so it is symmetric by construction. A corner crossing visits both neighbours (the cautious answer).
- A hand-built field without coarse regions (the test's ridge) is walked in full instead of inventing a grid; a new suite asserts the coarse pass and the bare walk agree on 2000 pairs.
- Field arrays are plain Lua arrays (the test reads `#field.height` and writes `nil` into it); per-tick world state will be the foreign arrays.
- `index`, `cell_of` and `reset_questions` are added to the contract table in `docs/014`.

Tested: `./run-tests` with the worktree as root; the phase 1 program on seeds 20260912, 1, 2, 3, 99 and 12345 (22 held, the other 10 suites absent by name, as expected); `./validate-documentation` (0 problems); `./compile --check-only` (13 files, 0 broken); 1000 seeds raised and validated.
